summary: The changed file (terraform/nsg.tf) introduces a well-structured NSG with defence-in-depth rules, a private-only Log Analytics workspace, AMPLS with Private Link, NSG diagnostic settings, and full DNS zone configuration for the TC01 research workload. The configuration demonstrates strong network isolation and private telemetry collection. One confirmed low-severity finding exists: the NSG's AllowSSHFromBastion rule permits destination_address_prefix '*', meaning SSH is allowed to any host in the associated subnet rather than a specific destination address. No policy violations are raised for controls explicitly scoped to production (DDoS, query paths) or for resource types with no applicable diagnostic categories.

findings.category_rationale: The AllowSSHFromBastion inbound rule uses destination_address_prefix = '*', which allows SSH (TCP/22) from the approved bastion source to any destination in the subnet rather than constraining it to a specific target host IP. This is a concrete, demonstrable overly-permissive scope in the configured rule, not a hypothetical concern.
findings.title: SSH allow rule uses wildcard destination, permitting access to any subnet host
findings.description: The inbound security rule 'AllowSSHFromBastion' at priority 300 restricts the source to the approved bastion address (203.0.113.10/32) but sets destination_address_prefix to '*'. In a subnet with multiple resources, this means a compromise of the bastion host — or a misconfiguration of the source prefix — could allow SSH to any resource in the subnet rather than only the intended target. Restricting the destination to the specific host IP or a named resource address reduces the blast radius of a lateral movement scenario.
findings.evidence: azurerm_network_security_group.nsg, security_rule 'AllowSSHFromBastion': source_address_prefix = '203.0.113.10/32', destination_address_prefix = '*', destination_port_range = '22', direction = 'Inbound', access = 'Allow', priority = 300.
findings.impact: If additional hosts are placed in subnet-demo (10.0.1.0/24) in the future, SSH is permitted from the bastion to all of them without any further rule change. In the current single-resource research context the risk is low, but the rule scope exceeds the documented intent of 'Administrative SSH from the approved bastion address'.
findings.recommendation: Set destination_address_prefix to the specific private IP address of the intended management target (e.g., '10.0.1.x/32') rather than '*'. This constrains the rule to its stated purpose and prevents implicit expansion as the subnet grows.

positives: NSG is associated with the subnet via azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association, satisfying NET-001.
The VNet uses dns_servers = [] (Azure DNS default), satisfying NET-002. The comment documents custom resolver intent without configuring a public DNS server.

NET-003 (DDoS Protection Standard) is explicitly scoped to production; main.tf and network.tf both establish this as a research workload (environment = 'research', research_case = 'PROM06-TC01'), and the network.tf comment explicitly references this exception. No finding is raised.

An explicit DenyAllInbound rule at priority 4096 and DenyAllOutbound rule at priority 4096 provide defence-in-depth before Azure's default allow rules (65000/65001), demonstrating intentional restrictive posture. These are correctly characterised as effective custom deny rules.
default_outbound_access_enabled = false on the subnet removes implicit outbound internet access at the subnet level, complementing the NSG outbound deny rule.

Log Analytics workspace has local_authentication_enabled = false, internet_ingestion_enabled = false, and internet_query_enabled = false, enforcing private-only telemetry paths consistent with SEC-001.

AMPLS is configured with ingestion_access_mode = 'PrivateOnly' and query_access_mode = 'PrivateOnly', and a private endpoint with all five required Azure Monitor DNS zones is provisioned and linked to the VNet, providing a complete private connectivity path for telemetry.

azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting.nsg enables both NSG diagnostic categories (NetworkSecurityGroupEvent and NetworkSecurityGroupRuleCounter) and forwards them to the private Log Analytics workspace, satisfying LOG-001 for this resource type.

All taggable resources (NSG, VNet, resource group, Log Analytics workspace, AMPLS, private endpoint, DNS zones) carry the mandatory tags (environment, owner, cost-center) plus the research_case identifier, satisfying TAG-001. The network.tf comment correctly notes that subnets do not support tags.

The 1 GB daily_quota_gb on the Log Analytics workspace is documented in the configuration context as a cost cap for the research scope; no policy or workload requirement specifies a minimum ingestion quota, so this is an acceptable operational tradeoff rather than a logging defect.

The 30-day retention_in_days on the Log Analytics workspace is noted for operational awareness. No supplied policy specifies a minimum retention period for this research workload, so no finding is raised.

Private DNS zone virtual network links are provisioned for all five Azure Monitor Private Link DNS zones with registration_enabled = false, which is appropriate for non-VM workloads and prevents unintended auto-registration.
final_recommendation: The NSG configuration is well-structured with strong network isolation controls. The single confirmed finding (F-001) is low severity and should be remediated by scoping the AllowSSHFromBastion destination_address_prefix to the specific management target IP rather than '*'. No policy violations were identified. The private telemetry architecture, defence-in-depth deny rules, and tagging are all correctly implemented for a research workload.
